scene.speaker: partner
scene.line: You found me at the hour when the work is done and the lamps aren't lit yet. I don't usually let anyone see me in the in-between.

scene.speaker: partner
scene.line: Sit. You don't have to fill the quiet. Most people do. I've started to notice that you don't.

scene.speaker: narrator
scene.line: They make room for you on the bench without being asked. The space is small. Neither of you moves to make it larger.

scene.speaker: partner
scene.line: There's a thing I tell almost no one. I'm going to tell you, and then we'll both pretend it was easy.

scene.speaker: partner
scene.line: When I was young I was certain I'd leave this place. I stayed. Most days I don't regret it. The days I do, I'd like you to be the one who notices.

scene.speaker: narrator
scene.line: They look at you for a long moment, as if checking the weight of the floor before trusting it. Then they let out a breath they seem to have been holding for years.

scene.speaker: partner
scene.line: I keep rehearsing a question and losing my nerve at the last word. So I'll say the part before it instead.

scene.speaker: partner
scene.line: Whatever you are building — the worlds, the work, the long strange life of it — I would like to be standing inside it. Not behind you. Beside.

scene.speaker: narrator
scene.line: They take your hand the way a mason sets a keystone: slowly, certain, as though everything afterward will rest on whether it holds. It holds.

scene.speaker: partner
scene.line: You again. That's twice this week you've turned up somewhere I didn't expect you.

scene.speaker: partner
scene.line: I'm not complaining. I only noticed. I notice more about you than I mean to, lately.

scene.speaker: narrator
scene.line: They say it lightly, already turning back to their work, but the corner of their mouth hasn't quite finished smiling.

scene.speaker: partner
scene.line: I've started setting out two cups instead of one. Force of habit, or maybe just hope wearing a habit's clothes.

scene.speaker: partner
scene.line: You take yours black, no sugar, and you always look faintly surprised that I remembered. I always will. That's not a small thing to me.

scene.speaker: narrator
scene.line: The kettle clicks off. Neither of you moves to answer it right away — the ordinary moment has become, somehow, worth staying inside.

scene.speaker: partner
scene.line: You went quiet on me for three days after the raid. I told myself it was nothing. It wasn't nothing.

scene.speaker: partner
scene.line: I don't need you to be fearless. I need you to tell me when you're not, instead of disappearing into it alone. Can you do that? Even the ugly parts?

scene.speaker: narrator
scene.line: It isn't a comfortable question, and you both know it. But they wait for your answer instead of filling the space for you — which is its own kind of trust.

scene.speaker: partner
scene.line: Good. Then we're actually building something, not just surviving next to each other.

scene.speaker: narrator
scene.line: Years, now, since the vows — long enough that the wedding feels like a story you both tell about two younger, more nervous people.

scene.speaker: partner
scene.line: I used to think devotion was a single moment you arrive at. It isn't. It's this — the field, the quiet, the two of us not needing to fill it with anything.

scene.speaker: partner
scene.line: I would choose this exact ordinary evening again, out of every evening there could have been. I wanted you to know that, plainly, before either of us forgets to say it.

scene.speaker: narrator
scene.line: The light goes gold and then gray. Neither of you moves to go inside. There is nowhere else, tonight, either of you would rather be.
